## Contract review

Reviewed at 2026-10-27T03:30Z — independent contract review of PR #26420 (card #26302, `skills/objectstack-platform`), rendered on head `f0926209` from `git show f0926209:PATH` against the spec and runtime on `origin/main` (tip `9a0108cd` at review time; the PR's merge base is `5507225e`). Adversarial by brief: not the dispatch order's conclusions, not the seat's, not the dev's report.

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f092620956fb037651f1300911515854c252ca4d`
Local-runs: probe — the two ratchet rows were recomputed by hand as ceil(bytes / 4) over `wc -c` of the `git show` blobs (the script's own documented hand audit) and the eval file was JSON-parsed from its blob; nothing was built, run or re-run
Scope: skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-platform/evals/config-plugins-ops.json, scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs + packages/spec/src/system/demo-staff.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/system/dev-login.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts (`demoStaff` / `devLogins` TSDoc, `collectDemoStaffErrors`, envelope keys), packages/spec/src/kernel/unmanaged-install.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts (`SEED_WRITE_EXECUTION_CONTEXT`), packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/demo-staff.ts, auth-plugin.ts, identity-write-guard.ts (+ its test), walled-owner-verification-path.ts (`devSeedAdminPassword`), dev-admin-seed-gate.ts, demo-staff-provisioning.test.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/dev.ts, build.ts, compile.ts, packages/cli/test/build-demo-staff-artifact.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts, app-plugin.seed.test.ts, app-plugin.seed-demo-staff.test.ts, docs/adr/0092-sys-user-profile-field-delegation.md, content/docs/references/system/demo-staff.mdx, dev-login.mdx, skills/objectstack-platform/references/bootstrap.md, operations.md, .github/workflows/lint.yml, ci.yml, .claude/agents/os-dev.md

Check-runs on `f0926209`, read once at 2026-10-27T03:21Z: 45 runs; 3 still `in_progress` — `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Test Core (1/8)`, `Test Core (2/8)`; every other run `success` or `skipped`. The gates this PR answers to: `Type Check · source gates` (hosts `check-skills-token-ratchet` + `--self-test`, `check:skill-docs`, `check:skill-refs` on the head's lint.yml) success; `Type Check · consumer gates` (`check:skill-examples`) success; `Lint · ESLint` success; `Lint · repo & tooling gates` success; `Lint · docs & code guards` success; `Build Core` (hosts `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, the dev's NOT-MEASURED family) success; `Check Changeset` success; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success (twice); `Part-of PR must not also close its card`, `The card this PR closes must claim this branch`, both single-writer guards success. Pending runs are reported as pending, not as green.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) Every new sentence against the spec and runtime on `origin/main`**

1. ⛔ **FALSE — "a `sys_user` row in `data` is refused (ADR-0092)"** (SKILL.md line 446; repeated by eval 7's expected output "no hand-written `sys_user` seed row (refused)"). The sentence copies the TSDoc of `packages/spec/src/system/demo-staff.zod.ts` lines 14–16, and that TSDoc is wrong against the platform it describes:
   - ADR-0092 D2 (lines 205–220) says the identity write guard "applies to user-context writes only"; "plugin system writes (`SYSTEM_CTX`) … bypass". `identity-write-guard.ts` `isUserContextWrite()` returns false for `isSystem: true`, and `identity-write-guard.test.ts` line 84 pins "bypasses system-context … writes" on `sys_user`.
   - Every seed insert runs under `SEED_WRITE_EXECUTION_CONTEXT` (`packages/spec/src/kernel/execution-context.zod.ts` line 630: `isSystem: true, skipTriggers: true, seedReplay: true`; `app-plugin.ts` line 56 `SEED_WRITE_OPTIONS`).
   - The runtime pins the row LANDING: `app-plugin.seed.test.ts` lines 43, 79, 113 and 290–327 seed `data: [{ object: 'sys_user', records: [...] }]` and assert `insert` was called with `'sys_user'`. `auth-plugin.ts` line 1656: "app seeds insert `sys_user` via raw engine.insert". `dev-admin-seed-gate.ts` lines 10–22 measured it end to end: "13 `sys_user` rows, zero `sys_account` rows, `POST /auth/sign-in/email` → 401" — a seeded person is "a directory row with no account", not a refusal.
   - ADR-0092 never mentions seed data in those words; its only `seed` reference (line 214) is the permission-set seed.
   The true reason the spec also gives — "it could not sign in anyway — signing in needs a hashed credential the auth pipeline mints" — is the clause the section dropped. An AI author reading the landed text expects a `sys_user` seed to fail at load; on the platform it lands silently as a dead row, which is the worse outcome and exactly the "who pays" the card names. A published teaching that states a refusal the platform does not perform is a falsehood under ①(a) — the same bar the sibling brief sets for a wrong parenthetical. **FAIL item.** Remedy (small): replace the reason with the true one, e.g. "a seed cannot create a person: a `sys_user` row written through `data` lands as a directory row with no account, so nobody can sign in as it"; drop "(ADR-0092)"; drop "(refused)" from eval 7's expected output (its assertions need no change); then re-measure both ratchet rows (the SKILL.md byte count will move; both rows must land again at headroom 0 and the row comments' byte arithmetic must be rewritten to match).

2. ✓ "A seed deals records to people (`owner_id: 'Legal Counsel 1'`) but cannot create one" — true (the dead-row measurement above; `demo-staff.zod.ts` `name` TSDoc; `collectDemoStaffErrors` duplicate-name message "Seed data deals a record to a person by name").
3. ✓ "Declare the people in `demoStaff`; `os dev` creates each account after the development admin" — `auth-plugin.ts` lines 1442–1446 register the `demoStaff` `kernel:ready` hook right after `maybeSeedDevAdmin`; `stack.zod.ts` line 1258 "after the development admin"; `demo-staff.ts` gate 2 explains why the order is load-bearing.
4. ✓ "signing in with the seed password (`--admin-password`, default `admin123`) — an entry carries no `password`" — `dev.ts` line 405 declares the `admin-password` flag and line 804 exports it as `OS_SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD`; `devSeedAdminPassword()` (`walled-owner-verification-path.ts` line 153) defaults to `'admin123'` and `maybeProvisionDemoStaff` (line 2501) hands exactly that to `provisionDemoStaff`; `DemoStaffSchema` is a `strictObject` with a `guidance.password` refusal, so `password` on an entry is refused at parse (pinned by `stack-demo-staff.test.ts` line 123), not merely absent. The sentence says "carries no `password`" — true either way.
5. ✓ The example entry parses: `name`, `email`, `position`, `permissionSets` are the four keys of `DemoStaffSchema`; it is a fragment inside a `typescript` fence, not `os:check`-marked, and `check:skill-examples` is green.
6. ✓ "`name` is what a seed reference resolves by" — `demo-staff.zod.ts` `name` TSDoc and `.describe()` ("the value a seed dataset names it by in a sys_user reference such as owner_id"); the generated `demo-staff.mdx` carries the same description.
7. ✓ "`position` / `permissionSets` name only what this stack declares (a platform set such as `admin_full_access` is refused)" — `collectDemoStaffErrors` (`stack.zod.ts` lines 4010–4057) resolves both against the stack's own `positions` / `permissions` (top level and assembled package bodies) at `defineStack` time; the refusal message says "never a platform set"; `stack-demo-staff.test.ts` line 152 pins `admin_full_access` as the refused spelling. Parse-time, which the section does not misstate.
8. ✓ "`os build` drops the key" — `build.ts` is an alias for `compile`; `compile.ts` line 1011 `delete finalBundle.demoStaff` at the one place the artifact is written; `build-demo-staff-artifact.test.ts` measures it by key, by text and through `loadArtifactBundle`. (The cheat sheet two screens down says `os compile`; both names are real.)
9. ✓ "a non-dev boot creates nothing" — `decideDemoStaffEnvironmentGate` refuses `NODE_ENV !== 'development'` (and migrate-and-exit, walled posture, non-loopback base URL) and `maybeProvisionDemoStaff` logs the refusal; `serve.ts` line 4366 hands the key over on every boot so the refusal is said, not silent. Precision, not a defect: the gate is narrower than "dev boot" (loopback base URL, `single` posture, an existing login) — "fewest lines" tolerates the elision.
10. ✓ "`devLogins` creates and grants nothing — it only prints an existing account on the boot banner" — `dev-login.zod.ts` "declaring an entry here CREATES NOTHING … presentation"; `guidance.permissions` "grants nothing — it only names an account for the boot banner to print"; `stack.zod.ts` line 1227. "Existing" is the intended use (the schema says an entry naming an account nothing seeds "prints a credential that does not work"), so the word is right as teaching.
11. ✓ The choice rule "Pick `demoStaff` whenever the demo needs an account to exist" follows from 3 and 10.

**(b) The cuts — duplicates with a surviving home (ruling A 「先削重复」), judged on the whole head SKILL.md**

1. ✓ `defineStack()` intro (two sentences: `objectstack.config.ts` is the entry point; it calls `defineStack()`). Home: head line 27–28 "Two concerns over one `defineStack()` / kernel surface: project setup (`objectstack.config.ts`, …)" and line 209 `objectstack.config.ts # ← THE entry point — defineStack()`. Both clauses survive.
2. ✓ "For the exact Zod shape … read `stack.zod.ts` … Each collection's item shape lives in its own domain folder" compressed to the pointer at head lines 78–80 (`ObjectStackDefinitionSchema`, the path, the domain folders all kept). The imperative "read the source" survives at lines 501–502 ("Always `Read` the source for exact field shapes"). Only the gloss "which keys are optional and what types the collection items take" is gone — that is what reading the schema answers, not a rule.
3. ✓ Boot step 6's aside "(see Ports & networking in Part 3)". Home: the **Port resolution** paragraph at lines 349–352 links `[Ports & networking](./references/operations.md#ports--networking)`.
4. ✓ Cheat-sheet comments "(auto-hops port if taken)" and "(see Ports & networking)". Home: the same paragraph — "dev hops to the next free port, production fails loudly" + the link; `operations.md` § Ports & networking (lines 61–74) carries the full rule. "pin the port explicitly" stays on the `os start` line.
No rule was lost; each cut is a restatement. Under the shared Acceptance ("nothing removed beyond the stale lines the card names") ruling A — the maintainer's own tap, newer — widens the licence to genuine duplicates, and these are.

**(c) Ratchet rows pinned at the measurement; ruling quoted where the script requires**

- Convention read off the script: `Math.ceil(Buffer.byteLength(text,'utf8') / 4)` (line 734), minus the release-stamp line's bytes for a stamped SKILL.md (line 785; hand audit on header line 111). Recomputed over the blobs: `origin/main` SKILL.md 23314 B − 20 B stamp line = 23294 B → 5824 tokens (ceiling 5828, headroom 4); head SKILL.md 23944 B − 20 B = **23924 B → 5981** (row 5981, headroom 0 ✓). Eval file `origin/main` 4842 B → 1211; head **5831 B → 1458** (row 1458, headroom 0 ✓). The row comments' arithmetic holds: 23294 − 309 + 939 = 23924; 4842 + 989 = 5831. Neither row carries smuggled headroom; neither is below the measurement.
- Raise rule (header lines 124–129): a raise "lands only in a PR whose body quotes a maintainer ruling". The PR body quotes the tap verbatim (「A:先削重复,余额按实测提高」, 2026-10-27T01:21Z, the card title) and so do both row comments. ✓
- `scripts/**` has no `max-len` rule in `eslint.config.mjs`; `Lint · ESLint` is green on the head. ✓
- Merge-base reconcile: `git diff origin/main f0926209 -- scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` against the merge base `5507225e` shows ONLY this PR's two rows and their comments ✓, and `01d2b0f8`'s SKILL.md and eval file are byte-identical to the merge head (only the ratchet script differs, by the sibling rows the merge of `5507225e` brought: ui #26295 ×5 rows, i18n #26388). Against `origin/main` NOW (`9a0108cd`), the head carries three STALE automation rows that #26390 (landed 2026-10-27T02:57Z, before the dev's merge commit at 2026-10-27T03:12Z, so the dev merged a stale `origin/main`) lowered since: `objectstack-automation/SKILL.md` 6004 (main 5780), `evals/flows-triggers-approvals.json` 1823 (main 1255), `references/state-machines-and-approvals.md` 5587 (main 5569). The PR did not touch those lines, GitHub reports `mergeable: true`, and a merge-method landing keeps main's values — so this is not a red gate, but it is why the head's ratchet script is not "main + two rows" today.

**(d) Eval**

- Eval 7: id unique and sequential (1–7), file JSON-parses, shape identical to the six fixtures (`prompt`, `expected_output`, `files: []`, `assertions`). `must_contain` ["demoStaff", "position", "permissionSets", "os dev"] all appear in the expected output. ✓
- Weakness, not a FAIL: `must_not_contain` ["role:", "admin_full_access"] names two strings the expected output itself writes in negation ("no `role:` alias, no platform set such as `admin_full_access`") — the exemplar answer trips its own assertions. The file already carries this pattern (eval 2's "data:beforeInsert" / "onInstall", eval 4's "@objectstack/adapter-"), so it is the inherited fixture convention, and no in-repo runner reads these files (`package.json` has no eval script; `skills/objectstack-data/evals/README.md` calls them "JSON fixtures in the objectui shape"). To-do for the seat below.
- The eval's "(refused)" parenthetical inherits the ①(a)-1 falsehood and goes with the fix.
- The card asks "one eval"; the new teaching has one. ✓

**(e) Card Wanted met, nothing beyond**

- One short section beside the bootstrap docs, `demoStaff` against `devLogins` ✓ — 19 lines under Seed Data, the section that owns `data:`, in the file that carries the package's only `devLogins` mention (line 49). The dispatch order allowed SKILL.md or `references/bootstrap.md`.
- Line 1 of SKILL.md untouched (PR #25640 owns it): the first 23 lines (whole frontmatter, stamp line `version: "18.1.0"` at line 20) are byte-identical to `origin/main`; the first hunk starts at line 33. ✓
- No file outside the claim's surface: three files; `references/_index.md` untouched (generator-owned; `check:skill-refs` green). ✓
- Line counts as the shared Acceptance demands, verified: SKILL.md 488 → 503; eval 65 → 75; package `.md` total (SKILL.md + references/**/*.md + rules/**/*.md, eight files) 2092 → 2107 (+15). The body's table matches. ✓

**(f) PR body**

- Line 1 the harness attribution HTML comment, line 2 `_Requested by_`, line 3 `Fixes #26302`, then `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` line-initial. `os-dev.md` line 323 is the exemption: "harness 自写的 PR 正文首行归属注释原样留、只报;`Fixes #N` 紧随其后" — the `_Requested by_` line is part of the harness block, and the two body-parsing guards (`Part-of PR must not also close its card`, `The card this PR closes must claim this branch`) are green, so the parsers read `Fixes` fine. ✓ No `Skills-docs:` line: `os-dev.md` line 279 owes it only for a non-`none` kind or `(narrowing)` — none owed, none written ✓ (the triage line's "Skills-docs: updated here" is a loose note, not the rule).
- `## 维护者速读` six labels in order; 需要你做的 = one action (Approve), right for Tier H; 先看 three items naming the hunks; 两分钟验证 one command — the script prints `tokens / ceiling (delta)` per row, so "headroom 都是 0" reads as `(+0)` on both platform rows — a fair paraphrase. English sections What changes / Tests / Acceptance notes / Verification present, readings folded in details blocks. Both readings (file and package lines, plus tokens) present. ✓
- The body's Tests section quotes six `defineStack` probes — all six consistent with `demo-staff.zod.ts` / `collectDemoStaffErrors` messages read here. The body's own "What changes" repeats the ①(a)-1 sentence ("a `sys_user` row in `data` is refused, ADR-0092") — amend with the fix.

**(g) Report and claim**

- os-dev-report 6432875949 (2026-10-27T03:17Z) carries `deviations` (6), `line_budget`, `out_of_scope_findings` (1), `mcp_calls: 2` (reads only), `api_writes: 2`; `files_changed` / `rules_retired` are not keys of the os-dev.md template on `origin/main` (lines 362–380), so not owed. Branch `claude/project-thread-sfzn7w` = the claim's `Branch:` line. ✓
- The report's `session` field spells out raw model identifiers ("session_context.model …") where the claim and the fleet's records use the tier name; the card comment is the dev's, not this record's, but it is a norm slip for the seat's roster.
- Commit `01d2b0f8`: author/committer os-warren (the reported override; the harness thread branch is not rewritten, AGENTS.md §3); both commit trailers model-free; no model name in either commit message or the PR body. ✓

### ② Semver level

`skip-changeset` is right: `skills/objectstack-platform/` has no `package.json`; `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` publishes nothing; no `.changeset/*.md` touched. `Check Changeset` green. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` line-initial in the body (and the claim). The skill teaches keys (`demoStaff`, `devLogins`) the protocol already carries since 18.2 / 17.5 — no protocol change, no `Skills-docs:` owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Card candidate (from ①(a)-1, widening the dev's class-c finding and reversing its direction):** `packages/spec/src/system/demo-staff.zod.ts` TSDoc (lines 14–16) states "a `sys_user` row written through `data` is refused (ADR-0092)", which the runtime does not do — a seeded `sys_user` lands as an account-less directory row (`dev-admin-seed-gate.ts`, `app-plugin.seed.test.ts`). `dev-login.zod.ts` guidance ("seed the account itself in `data`", "Seed the user record in the stack's `data` fixtures") describes a write that lands but produces a row nobody can sign in as — a prescription for the dead-row defect, now that `demoStaff` exists. One card: correct both spec texts to the measured behaviour and point `devLogins` guidance at `demoStaff`. Class c (spec prose vs runtime), reach: public teaching surfaces (`@objectstack/spec` TSDoc, generated reference docs are unaffected since they render `.describe()` only, this skill). Dedupe words: `demo-staff.zod.ts ADR-0092 refused seed sys_user TSDoc`, `seeded sys_user directory row no account`, `dev-login.zod.ts guidance seed data demoStaff`.
2. **Landing order:** two APPROVED reviews by os-zhuang on `f0926209` (2026-10-27T03:16Z), the PR readied and auto-merge armed before any contract review existed; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` passed twice before this record. os-zhuang is an authorized approver under the dispatch order's Tier H wording, so the approval itself is within the ruling — the sequence (approve, ready, arm, then review) is not what the Tier H text describes ("the seat runs the independent review; the maintainer's hand … lands it"), and with a FAIL record on the head the auto-merge should be disarmed by someone with the write (this record is read-only). If the queue took the PR before this posted, the record stands against head `f0926209` and the fix is a follow-up PR on the same card.
3. **Stale sibling rows** (①(c)): three automation rows on the head are older than `origin/main`'s; a merge-method landing resolves them to main's values. No action unless the landing is squashed onto a rebased head, in which case the rebase must take main's rows.
4. **Dev's deviations, verified:** 2 GitHub MCP reads before the ban was read (no writes; stated); author override on `01d2b0f8` (not rewritten, per AGENTS.md §3; the queue squashes); `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT-MEASURED locally — CI's `Build Core` hosts it and is green on the head; worktree cleaned (dev's word; not verifiable here).
5. Eval `must_not_contain` strings that the ideal answer writes in negation (①(d)) — a fixture-convention weakness across this file and the sibling files; a to-do for the skills lane, not a card.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-sfzn7w`
Reviewed-by: `session_01LqKsGyMNFwwnbF5FTAqyPn`

**VERDICT: FAIL** — ①(a) item 1: the new section's opening reason "a `sys_user` row in `data` is refused (ADR-0092)" (SKILL.md line 446, repeated as "(refused)" in eval 7 and in the PR body) teaches a refusal the platform does not perform; the runtime pins the row landing under the system seed context. Every other item passes (cuts, both ratchet rows at headroom 0, line counts, body shape, semver). Fix: reword the one sentence to the true reason, drop the ADR citation and the eval's parenthetical, re-measure the two rows, amend the body.
